dora-deane-or-the-east-india-uncle: Mary Jane Holmes was one of America's most popular storytellers of the 1800s, and this sentimental novel shows why. Young Dora Deane's life changes when a long-lost uncle returns from the East Indies, bringing fortune and upheaval to her modest world. Written for readers who loved tales of virtue rewarded, it is pure Victorian domestic drama.
victory-an-island-tale: Joseph Conrad's brooding novel follows Axel Heyst, a loner hiding from the world on a remote Malay island with the young woman he rescued. When three criminals land seeking his supposed treasure, his peace shatters into violence. A story of isolation, love, and moral failure, it ranks among Conrad's most haunting examinations of the human heart.
the-boy-ranchers-on-the-trail-or-the-dia: Willard Baker's boy ranchers ride out again, this time on the trail of cattle rustlers menacing the Diamond X ranch. Horseback chases, campfire councils, and narrow escapes fill a story built for young lovers of the West. Wholesome and action-packed, it delivers exactly the frontier excitement its readers craved.
the-swiss-family-robinson-told-in-words-: Lucy Aikin retells the beloved castaway adventure using only words of one syllable, so the youngest readers can manage it alone. The shipwrecked family's ingenuity — treehouse, farm, and all — unfolds in the simplest English. A clever, charming first book for children meeting a classic tale.
colonel-carter-of-cartersville: Francis Hopkinson Smith's beloved Virginian, Colonel Carter of Cartersville, wins every heart with old-Southern manners and grand, happy impracticality. These fond sketches of a true gentleman fallen on hard times made the Colonel famous across the land. Warm, funny, and full of local color.
mary-anerley-a-yorkshire-tale: R. D. Blackmore — beloved author of Lorna Doone — sets this tale among the dales and sturdy folk of Yorkshire. Mary Anerley's story of love and loyalty unfolds against a richly drawn rural England. Blackmore's gift for landscape and character shines throughout.
who-wrote-the-bible-a-book-for-the-peopl: Churchman Washington Gladden brings new Bible learning to plain readers, asking who truly penned the holy books. His fair, godly way helped the faithful take in hard study without loss of faith. A brave, clear landmark of broad-minded church thought.
robinson-crusoe-in-words-of-one-syllable: Defoe's great castaway tale retold so the youngest children can read it all by themselves — every word of one syllable. Crusoe's island ingenuity, his goats and grain, unfold in the simplest English. A brilliant first classic for beginning readers. Young readers meet the world's most famous castaway in language they can truly call their own.
a-prefect-s-uncle: Wodehouse's school farce introduces the prefect's alarming uncle — a former Oxford man whose unexpected arrival disrupts all order. Cricket, ragging, and comic chaos fill this early gem. Young Wodehouse already in glorious form. The result is schoolboy comedy of the most irresistible kind.
hawthorne-and-his-circle: Julian Hawthorne — the author's son — recalls his father Nathaniel and the great circle around him: Emerson, Longfellow, and the Concord luminaries. Intimate, affectionate, and full of literary gossip, it brings America's golden age vividly alive. A son's tribute and a biographer's treasure.
the-pilgrim-s-progress-in-words-of-one-s: Bunyan's immortal allegory retold so the youngest children can read it all themselves — in words of one syllable. Christian's flight from the City of Destruction to the Celestial City unfolds in the plainest English. A child's first great classic, made truly his own.
the-babylonian-story-of-the-deluge-as-to: Sir Wallis Budge tells how the Babylonian flood story was found — written on clay tablets at Nineveh, older than Genesis. His account of the discovery thrilled the world and reshaped ideas of the Bible's past. A landmark of archaeology, told by its hero.
my-tropic-isle: E. J. Banfield, the beachcomber of Dunk Island, records his life on a Great Barrier Reef isle — its birds, reefs, and Aboriginal neighbors. His gentle natural history is an Australian classic. A castaway's paradise, lovingly described. Turtles, trepang, and tropical birds fill this gentle island chronicle.
battle-studies-ancient-and-modern-battle: Colonel Ardant du Picq's Battle Studies — ancient and modern — probes what makes men fight: fear, honor, and comradeship. His unfinished masterpiece founded modern military psychology. A soldier's wisdom, profound and humane. His notes, found after his death, changed how armies understand men.
j-cole: Emma Gellibrand's J. Cole tells an Australian story — the author's own country writ with local truth. Her colonial tales preserve a vanished world. A rare early Australian woman's voice. Bush stations and colonial society live in her lively, observant prose.
stories-of-the-prophets-before-the-exile: Isaac Landman tells stories of the prophets before the exile — Elijah, Amos, Isaiah, and their fiery messages — retold for young readers. His vivid narratives bring the Hebrew prophets alive. Reverent, exciting Bible history for the young. Carmel's fire and Sinai's thunder sound through his retellings.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-font: This piece treats Fontenelle — Saint-Wandrille in Normandy, a house of ancient fame. Viking raids could not kill it for good. George Cyprian Alston traces its revivals. Norman piety at its best. The relics of Wandrille rest in its rebuilt church.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acacius-patri: This 1913 reference piece on Acacius, Patriarch of Constantinople — whose Henoticon split East from West. Cornelius Clifford explains the schism. Rome struck his name from the diptychs. Ambition's price, paid in schism. The schism named for him lasted thirty-five years.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aci-reale: A 1913 entry on Aci-Reale — the Sicilian diocese beneath Mount Etna. Its churches face the smoking peak. The entry gives its modern story. Faith in the volcano's shadow. Its carnival masks dance under Etna's smoke. The sea baths drew old Romans.
